newsitem.title: UK: Unicorn agrees on 85.5 mln stg buyout offer.
newsitem.headline: Unicorn agrees on 85.5 mln stg buyout offer.

text.p: British abrasives manufacturer Unicorn International said on Friday it had agreed on a recommended offer from France's Compagnie de Saint-Gobain valued at about 85.5 million stg.
The company will be taken over by Abrasives Plc, a wholly owned subsidiary of Compagnie de Saint-Gobain.
Unicorn, which has already given irrevocable undertakings to accept the offer in respect of 33.7 percent shareholding, said the offer valued each of its shares at 225 pence.
Unicorn's share price closed at 155 pence on Thursday. The offer price represents a 45 percent premium to the closing middle market quotation of Unicorn's share on Thursday.
Commenting on the sale, Unicorn's chairman Lindsay Bury said, "The market position and product range of Unicorn complements the existing abrasives businesses within the Saint-Gobain group".
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson is acting for the French company while Hambros is advising Unicorn in the deal.
